title: Laptops ask for credentials every time Teams opens
scenario: A laptop group loses its token after a restart: the number of affected laptops is corrected from three to eleven, a healthy device report turns into a missing one, and a client-side detour is tried before the cause is found.

events.title: Credentials prompt in Teams, Rotterdam
events.text: Hello. Three laptops in our Rotterdam office ask for credentials every time Teams is opened, since Friday evening. Examples from this morning: n.vos 07:12 UTC, k.dekker 07:40 UTC, s.jansen 08:05 UTC. Teams in the browser works for these users.

events.title: Re: Credentials prompt in Teams, Rotterdam
events.text: Hello, thanks for the information. Please run dsregcmd /status on one of the three laptops while the problem is there and paste the SSO State section here.

events.title: Re: Credentials prompt in Teams, Rotterdam
events.text:
Here is the output from n.vos's laptop:

| SSO State |
AzureAdPrt : YES
AzureAdPrtUpdateTime : 2026-07-13 06:58:11.000 UTC
AzureAdPrtExpiryTime : 2026-07-27 06:58:11.000 UTC

events.title: Re: Credentials prompt in Teams, Rotterdam
events.text: Thank you, that is useful. Please run the same command on the other two laptops and paste the output.

events.title: Re: Credentials prompt in Teams, Rotterdam
events.text: k.dekker and s.jansen both show AzureAdPrt : NO. One correction to my first email: I wrote three laptops, but the helpdesk now tells me eleven laptops are affected, all of them in Rotterdam and none in Utrecht.

events.title: Sign-in log lookup
events.text: Sign-in logs for n.vos 07:12, k.dekker 07:40 and s.jansen 08:05 UTC: a failed interactive sign-in row exists at each of those times, with error AADSTS50173, the grant has expired and a fresh authentication is needed.

events.title: Re: Credentials prompt in Teams, Rotterdam
events.text: Update: after a restart, n.vos's laptop shows AzureAdPrt : NO as well. It said YES this morning.

events.title: Re: Credentials prompt in Teams, Rotterdam
events.text: Understood. As a quick test, please clear the Teams cache on k.dekker's laptop and open Teams again.

events.title: Re: Credentials prompt in Teams, Rotterdam
events.text: I cleared the Teams cache on k.dekker's laptop and the credentials prompt is still there, exactly as before.

events.title: Re: Credentials prompt in Teams, Rotterdam
events.text: Thank you. Please also uninstall and reinstall Teams on s.jansen's laptop and open it afterwards.

events.title: Re: Credentials prompt in Teams, Rotterdam
events.text: Reinstalled Teams on s.jansen's laptop. The same prompt appears again.

events.title: Escalation
events.text: Thank you. I am escalating this to our identity backend team now, with the dsregcmd output and the sign-in log rows, and I will write again at 15:00 UTC with their answer.

events.title: Answer from the identity team
events.text: The identity team found that the device synchronisation from your on-premises directory has been paused since Friday evening, so the registration of those laptops stopped being refreshed. Please resume the synchronisation on the Entra Connect server and tell me when a cycle has completed.

events.title: Re: Answer from the identity team
events.text: The synchronisation was resumed at 16:20 UTC and a cycle completed at 16:32 UTC. I restarted the three laptops and they show AzureAdPrt : YES now.

events.title: Check after the synchronisation
events.text: Check at 16:50 UTC: the failure rate of the eleven laptops is zero since the restarts, and the pasted output of the three sample laptops shows AzureAdPrt : YES. I am closing the case.
